points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree in which, for any node, the left child is smaller than the parent and the right child is larger than the parent (smaller values to the left, larger to the right), in any wording.
points.partial_credit: Award 2-3 marks if the student says only that it is a binary tree (each node at most two children) or only that it is an ordered/sorted tree, without the left-smaller/right-larger rule; award 3-4 if the ordering rule is given but is vague or only half correct (e.g. only the left side stated).

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying it is a binary tree where left values are smaller and right values are larger than the parent, in any wording, however brief. Part marks for an answer with only half the idea, such as 'a tree with two children per node' or 'a sorted tree' without the left/right rule. No marks for unrelated descriptions. Extra correct detail or minor wrong remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the ordering rule.
